semantic_correction.stem: Which statement should a nurse include when teaching an adult about motor-vehicle injury prevention?

options.A: Use a seat belt mainly for highway travel because short local trips carry much less risk of serious crash injury.
options.B: Rear-seat adults may omit seat belts when the vehicle has front and side airbags because the airbags provide enough protection.
options.C: Wear a seat belt in every seating position on every trip because consistent restraint use substantially reduces serious injury and death.
options.D: Seat belts provide little additional protection in adulthood and are most important for children and adolescents.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC guidance updated January 27, 2026 states that seat-belt use is the most effective way to prevent injury or death in motor-vehicle crashes for adults and older children who are large enough for seat belts to fit properly. Seat belts reduce serious crash-related injuries and deaths by about half. CDC recommends using a seat belt in both front and back seats on every trip, no matter how short, and states that airbags provide added protection but are not a substitute for seat belts. Therefore option C is the appropriate adult injury-prevention teaching.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach adults to use a seat belt in every seating position on every trip because consistent restraint use substantially reduces serious crash injury and death and remains necessary even with airbags.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item directly tests current adult seat-belt teaching without a correct-answer length cue.

option_audit.A: Incorrect. CDC recommends seat-belt use on every trip, no matter how short.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Rear-seat adults also need seat belts, and airbags do not substitute for restraints.
option_audit.C: Correct. It matches CDC's every-seat/every-trip recommendation and adult injury-reduction evidence.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Seat belts are highly effective injury prevention for adults as well as older children.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. C alone matches all current CDC recommendations relevant to adult seat-belt use.
cueing_check: All four options are adult motor-vehicle safety statements of comparable length and specificity; no unique-length or absolute-word cue identifies C.
